preconditions.description: The number of stations n is between 3 and 3000 inclusive.
There are exactly n edges (passages) provided in the input.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= u <= n and 1 <= v <= n and u != v for u, v in edges)
preconditions.description: Each edge connects two distinct stations within the valid range [1, n].

preconditions.expression: len(set(tuple(sorted(e)) for e in edges)) == n
preconditions.description: No pair of stations has more than one passage between them.
The graph formed by stations and passages is connected (one can get from any station to any other).

postconditions.description: The output contains exactly n integers.
All distance values are non-negative integers.
Stations that are part of the unique ringroad have a distance of 0.

postconditions.expression: all(distances[i-1] == min_path_length(i, ring_nodes, edges) for i in range(1, n + 1))
postconditions.description: For every station i, the output value equals the minimum number of passages required to reach any station in the ringroad.
